item.research_question: How do cold-rolling and solution-treatment at 900 °C affect the microstructure and corrosion resistance of the non-equiatomic Fe36Mn20Ni20Cr16Al5Si3 HEA compared to SS304 in 0.6 M NaCl and NaCl solutions containing 0.5 M or 1 M H2SO4?
item.material_system: Fe36Mn20Ni20Cr16Al5Si3 (non-equiatomic HEA) and SS304 stainless steel
item.processing_route: Electric arc furnace casting (melted 4 times), cold-rolled to 86% area reduction ratio, and solution-treated at 900 °C for 30 min
item.test_conditions: Potentiodynamic polarization in 0.6 M NaCl, 0.6 M NaCl + 0.5 M H2SO4, and 0.6 M NaCl + 1 M H2SO4; surface analysis via SEM/EDX
key_findings: In 0.6 M NaCl, the cold-rolled condition showed the highest polarization resistance (Rp) of 33 kohm.cm², nearly three times that of the solution-treated condition (13.43 kohm.cm²).
The cold-rolled HEA had a corrosion current density (icorr) of 12.7 µA/cm² in 0.6 M NaCl, which is approximately one-ninth of the solution-treated condition (75.8 µA/cm²).
In 0.6 M NaCl + 0.5 M H2SO4, the solution-treated sample exhibited the best resistance with an icorr of 178.8 µA/cm², compared to 309.96 µA/cm² for the cold-rolled sample.
In 0.6 M NaCl + 1 M H2SO4, the cold-rolled sample's icorr increased to 563.1 µA/cm², while the solution-treated sample maintained a lower icorr of 101.18 µA/cm².
SS304 showed significantly worse performance in 1 M H2SO4 with an icorr of 2715 µA/cm² compared to both HEA conditions.
Localized pits in the cold-rolled condition were preferentially observed in areas containing BCC/B2 phase precipitates and intermetallics.
EDX analysis of corroded areas in 0.6 M NaCl showed relatively higher concentrations of Cr, Si, and Al compared to the bulk alloy composition.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that cold-rolling creates a stable passive film but leaves residual stresses and precipitates that act as initiation sites for localized corrosion in acidic media. Solution treatment relieves these stresses and homogenizes the microstructure, allowing for the formation of a more compact and stable passive film, particularly in the presence of H2SO4. However, the presence of Al-rich BCC phases and the formation of porous aluminum oxide films can negatively affect corrosion resistance by depleting Cr in the passive film, while Mn segregation can also reduce passivation capacity.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that the high entropy effect is not the only factor contributing to protection and that excessive Cr can lead to severe pitting due to segregation.
quotes: The corrosion test measurements revealed that cold-rolled Fe36Mn20Ni20Cr16Al5Si3 alloy is more resistant to corrosion in 0.6 M NaCl, while it is more susceptible to localized pits in H2SO4 to 0.6 M NaCl.
The solution-treated Fe36Mn20Ni20Cr16Al5Si3 HEA has the highest corrosion resistance compared to others with the addition of H2SO4 to 0.6 M NaCl.
Experimental results indicate that the pits are preferentially occurred in the areas of BCC/B2 phase precipitates.
